question: Card one on threat-v1: the research pass — steady, board-independent draw that survives a wipe?

contributions.slice: MODE prescribe: the branch's deck-audit, the captain's log, deck_recon.json
contributions.text:
Asked: of twenty-six researched cards, the ONE best upgrade to threat-v1 and the card it replaces. The answer is Black Market Connections for Midnight Reaper. The log's two loss shapes are wipes (001, 002, 006, cause `wipe` x3) and an empty hand by turns 8-10 (001, 002, 003, 006 — 'it is not a new finding, it is the finding, again'); the one win (008) was tokens converting through Blood Artist, Wispdrinker and Ashnod's Altar. The branch already closed the axes the other candidates aim at: by card_roles.json its 99 carries 11 removal-role cards (Anguished Unmaking, Boros Charm, Crackling Doom, Elspeth, Erebos, Liliana, Swords to Plowshares, The Meathook Massacre, Toxic Deluge, Vanishing Verse, Vish Kal), 2 sweepers and 7 protection-role cards (Akroma's Will, Boros Charm, Erebos, Giver of Runes, Selfless Spirit, Teferi's Protection, Yahenni), so Lethal Scheme, Damn, Winds, Everything Comes to Dust, Patron, Guardian of Faith and Clever Concealment close no measured gap. What the branch did NOT close is draw SHAPE. I enumerated every draw source among the 64 non-lands: Caretaker's Talent (a token enters), Welcoming Vampire (a power-2-or-less creature enters), Skullclamp (the equipped creature dies), Liliana (a creature dies), Morbid Opportunist (a creature dies), Erebos (a creature dies, 2 life), Crossway Troublemakers (an attacking Vampire dies), Midnight Reaper (a NONTOKEN creature dies), Twilight Prophet (upkeep, once ascended — on a body), Bloodtithe Harvester and Anje (Blood tokens: a rummage, not a card), and three tutors (selection, not advantage). Every one of them is on-plan or on a creature; the only board-independent draw left in the branch is a land, Castle Locthwain, because the branch traded Phyrexian Arena for Skullclamp. That is exactly the stacked shape strategy:card-advantage.plan-draw says empties a hand at turn 7-8, and it fails hardest in the state the log keeps recording: after a wipe, with nothing to cast. Black Market Connections is the one candidate that is steady draw AND rebuilds the fuel: each first main phase a card, a Treasure, and a 3/2 changeling token — a Vampire body that enters (Elas gains 1, so Vito, Sanguine Bond, Enduring Tenacity and Blight-Priest drain; Caretaker's Talent and Anje trigger) and then dies to any of the branch's eight outlets into eight each-opponent death drains. It is an enchantment, so the wipe that kills the fodder leaves it; it needs no Edgar; the life it costs is the resource the drain engine refunds. The taxonomy files it ramp:treasure/threat:tokens, so the audit's card-advantage count will not move — the oracle text does the job the count cannot see. Midnight Reaper is the cut because the branch has already ruled on its shape: Grim Haruspex was cut on 2026-11-13 because it 'draws only on nontoken deaths', and Reaper reads the same clause while also costing a life per card; the deck's deaths are tokens, which Reaper never sees. It is also a cheap non-Vampire — 'a cheap non-Vampire is only a body' is the thesis's own words. Not the goldfish: the pilot ruled it out, and no goldfish figure appears here.
